## Definition and typical features 
These studies aim to identify methods that can address a specific research challenge. It often combines identification with a structured characterisation or comparison of methods, for example by describing definitions, key features, variants, assumptions, strengths, or limitations.

## Boundaries to related purposes

## Typical approaches and corresponding examples 
[Scoping review of methods research](../approaches/11scoping-review.qmd): identify causal methods to allow predictions under hypothetical interventions;[@Lin2021a] identify definitions of intention-to-treat;[@Alshurafa2012inconsistent] review of causal methods to allow predictions under hypothetical interventions;[@Lin2021a] identify criteria for assessing the credibility of subgroup analyses;[@Schandelmaier2019a] identify factors influencing the trustworthiness of non-randomized studies;[@Adegboye2025factors] identify methods addressing bias in adaptive trial designs.[@Robertson2023point]; 

[Review of applied methods](../approaches/9review-applied.qmd): to identify types of initial data analysis in observational studies.[@Huebner2020hidden]
